_comment: This is documentation, not a real record. Every file in this folder (except this one) must follow this exact shape. Fields left as null mean 'this condition does not apply / is not used to screen this opportunity' and are skipped by the rules engine. Fields added 2026-09-11: gender_required, min_english_level, min_computer_skills, fields_of_study (gates) and priority_groups (advantage only, never a gate).
name: string, official program name
category: one of: scholarship | job | skills | assistance
province_scope: one of: Balochistan | Punjab | Sindh | KP | AJK | GB | ICT | Federal | Nationwide
target_group: short string, who this is generally for

eligibility_conditions.domicile_provinces: list of province strings or null (null = no domicile restriction)
eligibility_conditions.min_education_level: one of: matric | intermediate | bachelor | master | null
eligibility_conditions.employment_status_required: one of: unemployed | employed | any | null
eligibility_conditions.special_quota_note: string or null, e.g. exemptions for orphans / BPS 1-4 govt employees' children
eligibility_conditions.min_experience_years: number or null, used for job/category=job entries only
eligibility_conditions.deadline_is_provisional: true when application_deadline is a placeholder for an expected cycle rather than an announced date. The UI labels it as provisional.
eligibility_conditions.enrolment_is_continuous: true when the programme accepts applications all year and there is no closing date to miss. NOT the same as leaving application_deadline null, which means 'we do not have a date' - the UI tells a user to go and check in that case, and tells them there is nothing to miss in this one. Set this only when the programme genuinely never closes; if it is also given a real deadline, the deadline wins.
eligibility_conditions.application_deadline: YYYY-MM-DD or null, used for job/category=job entries only (jobs go stale - always check this)
eligibility_conditions.gender_required: one of: female | male | any | null (null = no gender restriction). Use only when the programme genuinely reserves places by gender.
eligibility_conditions.min_english_level: one of: none | basic | intermediate | fluent | null
eligibility_conditions.min_computer_skills: one of: none | basic | intermediate | advanced | null
eligibility_conditions.fields_of_study: list of study fields the programme is restricted to, or null (null = open to all fields). Allowed values are listed in core/models.FIELDS_OF_STUDY
eligibility_conditions.priority_groups: list of groups this programme gives PRIORITY to, or null. An ADVANTAGE ONLY - never used to exclude anyone. Allowed: female | disability | orphan | minority | under_served_district. Only add a group if the official source actually states it.
eligibility_conditions.required_groups: list of groups this programme is RESTRICTED to, or null. A GATE, unlike priority_groups above - use it only where the group IS the eligibility, such as an orphans' home or a disability stipend. Read as OR: belonging to any one of them qualifies. Allowed values are ONLY female | disability | orphan, because nothing in a non-identifying profile can establish religion or district; gating on minority or under_served_district would create an UNKNOWN no user could ever resolve. An unanswered profile field produces 'unknown' (a question), never 'unmet' (a rejection).

official_url: string, must be a real official URL
source_title: string, name of the page/document this was sourced from
source_date: YYYY-MM-DD, date the source page/document itself was published or last updated, if known
last_verified: YYYY-MM-DD, date a human on the team actually checked this record against the official source
disclaimer: string shown with this specific entry, if it needs one beyond the global banner
